t.1.29.1: Then those two princes, subduers of foes, who knew what befits place and time and were skilled in speech suited to place and time, spoke these words to Kauśika.
t.1.29.2: O blessed one, we two wish to hear at what time those two night-roaming demons are to be guarded against, O brahmin, so that the moment may not slip past.
t.1.29.3: As the two Kākutsthas spoke thus, hastening in their eagerness to fight, all those sages, delighted, praised the two sons of the king.
t.1.29.4: From this day onward, for six nights, you two, O Rāghavas, must keep guard, for this sage has entered upon his consecration and will observe a vow of silence.
t.1.29.5: Having heard those words, the two illustrious princes, without sleep, guarded the penance grove for six days and nights.
t.1.29.6: The two heroes, those supreme archers, sat in attendance, and those subduers of foes guarded Viśvāmitra, the foremost of sages.
t.1.29.8: While Rāma, hastening with eagerness for battle, was speaking thus, the sacrificial altar, together with the upādhyāyas and the purohitas, then blazed up.
t.1.29.9: That sacrifice proceeded duly, with the proper mantras, as prescribed; and in the sky there arose a great and terrifying sound.
t.1.29.10: Just as a cloud that has risen in the rainy season covers the sky, so the two Rākṣasas, working their sorcery, rushed forward to the attack.
t.1.29.11: Mārīca and Subāhu, and likewise their followers, terrible in appearance, came and let loose torrents of blood.
t.1.29.7: Then, when that time had passed and the sixth day had arrived, Rāma said to Saumitri, "Be vigilant and composed."
t.1.29.12: Seeing those two rushing swiftly toward him, lotus-eyed Rāma looked intently at Lakṣmaṇa and spoke these words.
t.1.29.13: Look, Lakṣmaṇa, at these wicked, flesh-eating rākṣasas, scattered by the Mānava weapon as clouds are scattered by the wind.
t.1.29.14: Rāghava, supremely enraged, hurled the Mānava weapon, supremely mighty and supremely radiant, at the chest of Mārīca.
t.1.29.15: Struck by that supreme Mānava weapon, he was hurled a full hundred yojanas into the surging waters of the ocean.
t.1.29.16: Seeing Mārīca unconscious, whirling about, struck by the force of the cold arrow, and hurled far away, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa:
t.1.29.17: Look, Lakṣmaṇa: the cool Mānava arrow, imbued with dharma, stuns him and carries him away, yet he is not parted from his life.
t.1.29.18: These too I shall slay, the pitiless rākṣasas of wicked conduct, steeped in sinful deeds, destroyers of sacrifices, drinkers of blood.
t.1.29.19: Taking up the very mighty fire-missile, Raghunandana hurled it at the chest of Subāhu; pierced by it, he fell to the ground.
t.1.29.21: Having slain all the rākṣasas who were destroyers of the sacrifice, Raghunandana was honored there by the ṛṣis, just as Indra was of old upon his victory.
t.1.29.20: Taking up the Vāyavya weapon, the greatly renowned and supremely noble Rāghava slew the remaining ones, and so joy was brought to the sages.
t.1.29.22: Then, when the sacrifice had been completed, the great sage Viśvāmitra, seeing the quarters free from calamities, spoke these words to Kākutstha.
t.1.29.23: I have achieved my purpose, O mighty-armed one; you have fulfilled your guru's word. O Rāma of great fame, you have made this Siddhāśrama true to its name.
